data.question: General Multiplication = Moduli Multiply, Arguments Add: the Checking Bench
data.explanation: This step answers: multiplying by an arbitrary complex number — what happens to modulus and to angle? First verify the two halves separately: multiplying by a positive real (preset 2 below) only scales and never turns; multiplying by a number of modulus 1 only turns and never scales. An arbitrary multiplier z₂ stacks the two. Drag z₁ (the multiplicand) and z₂ (the multiplier); the green arrow is the product z₁·z₂. The bench below checks three groups, all computed live: the modulus check, the angle check, and an algebraic route (a₁a₂ − b₁b₂, a₁b₂ + b₁a₂) — two roads, one source, cross-verified.
data.scope: Conclusion: the multiplication law — moduli multiply, arguments add. Multiplying by a number scales you by its modulus and rotates you by its argument. Conditions, stated: after adding, angles must be normalised into the principal interval (340° and −20° are the same direction; this page writes −20°); if either factor is 0, the product is the origin and has no argument.

data.arg: Angle check: θ₁ + θ₂ = 26.6° + 0°, normalised to the principal value = 26.6°; the product’s argument = 26.6° ✓ equal
data.algebra: Algebraic route: (a₁a₂ − b₁b₂, a₁b₂ + b₁a₂) with each component substituted = (2×2 − 1×0, 2×0 + 1×2) = 4 + 2i, matching the product point’s coordinates ✓
